title: Edit an existing Gmail draft with AI without sending it
h1: revise a gmail draft without starting over
description: Tell your bot “shorter” and get a better Gmail draft. Keep the recipients and subject, with every attachment added again when the message is rebuilt.
answer:
**say "shorter" instead of rewriting the email yourself.** a bot can revise a saved gmail draft's wording, subject or recipients. it updates the draft without sending it.

every edit rebuilds the message, so attachments need adding again. ask for a proposed revision if you want to read it before the saved draft changes.

review.by: lead agent, after two independent reviewer passes, against Metal docs and the composio catalog

what:
**keep the proposal attached while you cut the waffle.** the bot replaces the draft's message. recipients, subject and body stay as they were unless you ask to change them. files need adding again, even for a one-word edit.

have it retrieve the existing attachments first and stop if one is missing. a shorter email still needs the proposal it promises.
uses: **cut a long proposal.** keep the pricing pdf attached while shortening the wording.
**fix the introduction before sending.** correct its recipient and subject on the saved draft.
**use the confirmed delivery date.** replace the tentative one without rewriting everything.
**finish the sign-off.** ask it to add your configured gmail signature.

routine.message:
each wednesday at 3, find gmail drafts about kiln deliveries created or changed during the past week. show each recipient and subject, then propose a shorter body here. ask me before updating any draft.

keep its recipients and subject. retrieve and reattach every existing file; stop if one is unavailable. skip drafts that need no change. never send or edit unrelated drafts.
routine.needs: gmail read and write, limited to draft listing, updating and required file retrieval
routine.output:
proposed revision for noor at willowquay ceramics

subject: kiln delivery
body: delivery is confirmed for thursday. handling notes attached.
file to keep: kiln-handling.pdf

read this version before it replaces the saved draft.

steps: **allow draft edits.** connect gmail with read and write, restricted to the needed actions.
**find the saved message.** list drafts with full details, including recipient, subject and files.
**ask for the revision first.** say which parts stay, and require every attachment again.
**open the saved result in gmail.** look at the recipients and attachments, then try recurring edits. pause if it picks the wrong draft.
watch: **the files must go back in.** keeping the recipient or subject does not preserve attachments.
**show everyone on the email.** ask for the full recipient list after the edit, including copies.

faq.q: will old attachments survive a wording change?
faq.a: **only if the bot adds them again.** tell it to stop if a file is missing.

faq.q: can it change the draft without asking?
faq.a: **yes, if you allow draft updates.** put a review step in the request; draft edits do not ask automatically.

steps: choose one saved draft with an attachment
ask for a shorter version, without saving
require the same recipient, subject and files
allow the edit, then inspect the attachment

worked.intro: invented draft, with a made-up sender and customer
worked.before:
noor writes to willowquay ceramics: please see the attached delivery notes. i am writing to confirm that the delivery date is thursday.
file: delivery-notes.pdf
worked.after:
proposed body: delivery is confirmed for thursday. notes attached.

same recipients and subject. delivery-notes.pdf added again. ready to read in gmail.

mistakes.fix: open the attachments too. replacing a draft does not keep them automatically.

mistakes.mistake: editing the same old proposal every week
mistakes.fix: review new or changed drafts. skip anything that needs no revision.

tip.text: open the file before admiring the shorter sentence.
